title: Just-in-Time Memory: Learning to Curate Task-Adaptive Memory for LLM Agents
authors: Yefan Zhou, Yang Li (equal contribution), Zeyu Leo Liu, Semih Yavuz, Shafiq Joty
date: 23 September 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version on 3 October 2026)

code.title: no code released
code.note: neither the paper nor its arXiv page links code, trained curator weights or trajectories (checked 3 October 2026); the prompts are printed in full in Appendix A

takeaway: Curating an agent's memory at read time, once the task is known, beats distilling trajectories at write time by 16.2 and 16.3 points on ALFWorld and WebShop, and an untrained curator already wins, so the gain is the timing rather than the model.
verdict: Believe the direction, not the headline's attribution. Untrained read-time curation beats untrained write-time memory with the same model in 15 of 17 comparisons, but the +16.2 and +16.3 come mostly from RL training (92% of the WebShop gain; the trained curator with no memory at all already beats every baseline there), 36 of the 60 baseline cells are SkillOS's published numbers rather than reruns, and the tau2-bench +3.9 is under two standard errors.

headline.k: over the strongest baseline, ALFWorld and WebShop
headline.d: RL-trained JitMem against RL-trained SkillOS, Qwen3-8B executor

headline.k: untrained read-time beats untrained write-time, same curator model

resources.t: SkillOS: Learning Skill Curation for Self-Evolving Agents
resources.n: the closest prior work: an RL-trained write-time skill curator that needs grouped task streams for its delayed reward. Its Tables 1 and 2 are the source of most of JitMem's baseline rows.

resources.t: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
resources.n: the strongest heuristic write-time baseline: distil each trajectory into at most three strategy items, retrieve by embedding similarity. JitMem's 'w/o raw traj.' ablation uses its distillation prompt.

resources.by: Fang et al., Findings of ACL 2026
resources.n: the third baseline: procedural memory items at several granularities, built, retrieved and updated at write time.

resources.t: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed
resources.n: the same read-time idea, but one GRPO policy both adapts the retrieved experience and executes the task, so it cannot be moved to another executor; JitMem's separate curator can.

resources.t: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
resources.n: the origin of write-time verbal memory: after a task, write a reflection and reuse it next time.

resources.t: Decocted Experience Improves Test-Time Inference in LLM Agents
resources.n: query-independent lesson distillation; the source of the paper's 'higher information density, more efficient completion' reading of Table 4.

resources.t: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective (Dr. GRPO)
resources.n: why JitMem drops GRPO's standard-deviation normalisation of advantages.

resources.t: ALFWorld: Aligning Text and Embodied Environments for Interactive Learning
resources.n: the household benchmark; the 140 'valid_seen' games are the test set, six task types. This page's stream replay uses their real goal texts.
where the 140 test goals on this page come from (valid_seen, solvable games).

resources.t: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents
resources.n: the shopping benchmark: 500 test instructions, a 0 to 100 attribute-match score, and success when the score is 100.

resources.t: tau2-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
resources.n: the airline, retail and telecom customer-service benchmark used without training in Table 2.

kb.t: Proactive Memory Agent: selective reminding for long-horizon agents
kb.n: decides when to remind an agent of something it already holds, inside one task; JitMem cites it as arXiv 2607.08716 (Wu et al. 2026b) and contrasts in-session with cross-task memory.

kb.t: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
kb.n: context compaction found by an auto-research loop: it shrinks what is carried forward, the opposite design choice to keeping trajectories raw.

kb.t: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
kb.n: the same just-in-time move one level up: synthesise the harness itself per task at inference time instead of fixing it in advance.

kb.t: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work, Until They Don't
kb.n: finds skills distilled from the same trajectories beat raw workflow memory handed to the agent. JitMem never hands raw traces to the executor either: it distils them, just later.

kb.t: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
kb.n: write-time distillation at library scale: knowledge fixed into skills before any task asks for it.

kb.t: Trained Persistent Memory for Frozen Encoder-Decoder LLMs
kb.n: memory folded into a fixed latent bank at write time, with the write rule untrained; the opposite end of the design space from raw storage.

kb.t: End-to-End Context Compression at Scale (Latent Context Language Models)
kb.n: query-independent compression of context, learned end to end: what JitMem argues against for cross-task memory.

kb.t: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch
kb.n: an append-only raw record as shared memory: keep everything, decide what matters when it is read.

kb.t: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
kb.n: the reason-then-act executor loop and the original agent results on ALFWorld and WebShop.

kb.t: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
kb.n: the general pattern underneath: store raw, retrieve at query time, let the reader condition on the query.
where GRPO, the group-relative advantage JitMem trains its curator with, was introduced.

topics.n: memory as a harness component; this paper argues for raw storage and read-time compute over compaction-first designs.
BM25 over task descriptions, and what a retriever-plus-curator adds over retrieving fixed artifacts.
GRPO on a single immediate reward: a curator trained from task success with a frozen executor.
credit assignment: the paper's case is that read-time curation turns a delayed, many-task reward into a one-step one.
